s1.syndrome_frame: A lesion on the glans penis with a short time course, characterized by an irregular and friable mass, with primary syndrome of a potentially malignant tumor, and alarm context of lymphovascular invasion
salient_findings: 2 × 2 cm irregular, friable mass on the glans penis
Nearly complete epidermal ulceration with replacement by an in-situ and diffusely infiltrative atypical clear cell tumor
key_facts: 78-year-old man
History of diabetes mellitus
History of hypertension
History of moderately differentiated prostatic adenocarcinoma without evidence of metastasis
History of nodular basal cell carcinoma
Lesion on the glans penis
2 × 2 cm irregular, friable mass on the glans
Deep shave biopsy showed nearly complete epidermal ulceration
Tumor consisted of large irregular nests and lobules of clear cells
Abundant multivacuolated cytoplasm, nuclear indentations, and vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei
Lymphovascular invasion present
Diffuse pagetoid spread within the epidermis

s4.champion: Primary clear-cell carcinoma of the penis

raw.champion: Primary clear-cell carcinoma of the penis
raw.rationale: The presence of a tumor with clear cells, abundant multivacuolated cytoplasm, nuclear indentations, and vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei, along with diffuse pagetoid spread within the epidermis and lymphovascular invasion, is most consistent with primary clear-cell carcinoma of the penis, especially given the location on the glans penis and the absence of known metastasis from other clear-cell primary sites.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the penis
rejected.why: While possible, the specific clear-cell features and pagetoid spread are not typical for standard squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Clear cell squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This option is less specific and does not fully account for the clear-cell features described.

rejected.label: Metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: There's no mention of a primary renal cell carcinoma, making this less likely without further evidence of a renal primary tumor.

rejected.label: Extramammary Paget's disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with different cytological features, such as pagetoid cells that are usually smaller and have a distinct nucleocytoplasmic ratio, and it doesn't fully explain the clear-cell features described.
